extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) preparing PTAB appeal briefs
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and required elements for drafting effective appeal briefs to the USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Focuses on argument selection, organization, evidence, addressing examiner errors, and required brief sections under 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present Strong Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Present only the strongest arguments. Do not dilute strong arguments by including weaker arguments or arguments that have no bearing on the issues. Do not simply repeat arguments previously presented because those have already been evaluated and deemed unpersuasive by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and present a limited set of your best arguments; omit weak or irrelevant points; avoid repeating arguments already made during prosecution that the examiner found unpersuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: You generally want the PTAB to read your strongest arguments first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue the most glaringly incorrect rejection(s) first — you don't have to start with the rejection of Claim 1. Order sections so the panel encounters your best points up-front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argue Claims Separately
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB will not evaluate the patentability of any claims not individually addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separately argue as many dependent claims as possible; place such arguments under separate sub-headings for ease of readability; identify which claims rise/fall together; group claims thoughtfully to make it clear which claims are being challenged and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support with Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney argument cannot substitute for evidence. Cite evidence to support arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any relied-upon evidence in the appeal brief must have been before the examiner during prosecution for the PTAB to consider it. Provide citations to the prosecution record and any admissible evidence rather than relying solely on attorney assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Examiner Errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispute factual errors and legal errors made by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and explain errors such as: claim and reference misinterpretations; citations of non-analogous art; improper combinations under §103; failure to provide reasoned rationale (KSR); failure to address all claim limitations. Show why the examiner's findings are incorrect and support with evidence/precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Section: Real party in interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include identification of the real party in interest as a discrete section of the appeal brief per 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals, interferences, and trials (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Section: Related appeals, interferences, and trials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any related appeals, interferences, or trials in a dedicated section as required by 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Section: Summary of claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary of the claimed subject matter so the Board can quickly understand the invention and claim scope, as required by 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the substantive legal and factual arguments addressing the grounds of rejection in a clearly organized Argument section, per 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a claims appendix containing the claims at issue to facilitate review, as required by 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix (if applicable) (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an evidence appendix containing any evidence relied upon (that was before the examiner), when applicable, in accordance with 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings appendix (if applicable) (Required Section under 37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Section: Related proceedings appendix (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, include an appendix identifying related proceedings, per 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep arguments concise and focused
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary verbosity; present focused, tightly reasoned arguments that directly address the rejection and relevant claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claim charts to compare prior art with claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use claim charts to compare prior art with claim language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ claim charts to show element-by-element comparisons between prior art references and claim limitations to clarify distinctions or show lack of teaching/ motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address each rejection as a separate ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Address each rejection as a separate ground
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the brief so each rejection is treated independently and responded to as a separate ground, improving clarity and ensuring the Board can evaluate each basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite controlling precedent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support legal arguments with controlling case law and PTAB/ Federal Circuit precedent to strengthen legal positions and explain why the examiner's conclusions are legally incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid emotional or accusatory language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use inflammatory, emotional, or accusatory wording in the brief; focus on reasoned legal and factual argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional tone toward examiner
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use respectful, professional language throughout; preserve professionalism even when pointing out examiner errors.
